name: MonarchEventChip
title: EventChip
summary: One event in a calendar view: a color dot or bar, the title, the time and the status, as a button that opens the event or as a label.
whenToUse: For an event in a month cell, an agenda row, an all-day row or a time grid, where tapping it opens the event.
whenNotToUse: For a list of events with more detail per row use a Material 3 ListItem. For a status alone use MonarchBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchEventChip(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchEventChipVariant = MonarchEventChipVariant.Dot, status: MonarchEventChipStatus = MonarchEventChipStatus.Confirmed, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, past: Boolean = false, compact: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, time: String? = null, timeLabel: String? = null, detail: String? = null, statusLabel: String? = null, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchEventChipVariant { Dot, Bar, Block }
enum class MonarchEventChipStatus { Confirmed, Tentative, Cancelled, Declined }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component. Give a Block chip its size here.

options.name: color
options.description: The event's color, for the marker, the border and the tint only. Unspecified is the theme's accent.

options.name: past
options.description: The event has ended: muted title and a faded marker.

options.name: compact
options.description: A Block chip on one line, time then title, without the status word and the detail.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether onClick can be triggered. The look does not change.

options.name: time
options.description: The visible time, already formatted. Leave it out for an all-day event in an all-day row.

options.name: timeLabel
options.description: The time as TalkBack reads it when time is abbreviated, such as "9:30 to 10:15" or "All day".

options.name: detail
options.description: A second, muted line in Bar and Block chips.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the status (monarch_eventchip_tentative, _cancelled, _declined), in the visible word and in what TalkBack reads.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the event. With it the chip is a button; without it a label.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions.

states.name: confirmed
states.description: A filled dot or a solid bar; Bar and Block chips have a light tint of the event color (14% over the surface).

states.name: tentative
states.description: A hollow dot or a dashed bar, a lighter tint (6%) and a border in the event color. The status word is drawn in Bar and Block chips and read in all.

states.name: cancelled, declined
states.description: Muted text, the title struck through, the marker in the strong border color (a ring in a Dot chip) and the muted fill instead of the tint. The status word is drawn in Bar and Block chips and read in all.

states.name: past
states.description: Muted title and the marker mixed 45% towards the surface color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: With an action: a Dot chip gets the muted fill, a tinted chip a stronger tint (22%), a cancelled chip the emphasis fill. A ripple is drawn too.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false stops the action and TalkBack says it is disabled. The look does not change.

appearance: Text uses the default and muted text roles in every theme; the event color (or the accent) is only the marker, the border of a tentative chip and a tint mixed into the surface color. Cancelled and declined chips use the muted background and the strong border color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes change the roles; the event color is the app's.
platformNotes: The same statuses, variants and compact density as the web and iOS. The web chip is always a button or a link; here, as on iOS, the action is optional, and a link is an onClick that opens the URL. The web's asChild is not needed. The web tints with color-mix; here the event color is mixed into the surface color with lerp at the same ratios, and the faded past marker is mixed towards the surface rather than drawn with opacity, because Monarch does not dim with alpha. With an action the chip reserves a 48dp touch target in the layout (the web uses 24px on touch screens, iOS 44pt), so chips stacked in a small month cell need that room.
accessibility: One TalkBack element whose content description is "title, time, status, detail". The status is left out when confirmed and the detail in a Dot chip; the texts inside are not read separately.
timeLabel replaces the visible time in what TalkBack reads.
With an action the element has the Button role and a touch target of at least 48dp reserved in the layout; the visible chip stays compact inside it.
The status is never color alone: a hollow or dashed marker, a struck-through title, and the status word.
The text grows with the font size setting. From font scale 1.3 the title of a Dot chip wraps instead of ending with an ellipsis.
The color bar is at the start edge and moves to the right edge in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A Block chip fills the size it is given and clips what does not fit. A Block chip under 48dp high with an action cannot reserve its touch target; give it at least 48dp.
A long title in a Dot chip ends with an ellipsis at standard font sizes; TalkBack still reads all of it.
In a Bar chip the time and the status move under the title when they do not fit on one line.
past is not read; the time already says when the event was.
An empty title leaves the spoken name to the time and the status.

examples.title: Dot chips (month cell)
An agenda row that opens the event
examples.code:
MonarchEventChip(
    title = "Design review",
    variant = MonarchEventChipVariant.Bar,
    color = MonarchTheme.colors.successSolid,
    time = "14:00 – 15:00",
    timeLabel = "2 to 3 in the afternoon",
    detail = "Room 4",
    onClick = { open = true },
)

examples.title: A block in a time grid
examples.code:
MonarchEventChip(
    title = "Workshop",
    modifier = Modifier.height(96.dp),
    variant = MonarchEventChipVariant.Block,
    time = "10:00 – 12:00",
    detail = "Lab",
)
